newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikkei average to rise above 20,000 in H2--analyst.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei average to rise above 20,000 in H2--analyst.

text.p: Japan's key stock index is likely to rise above 20,000 in the second half of this year, prompted by a recovery in the economy, Credit Suisse First Boston Bank strategist Taisuke Tanaka said in a commentary.
He predicted in the commentary, issued earlier this week, that the economic recovery would take place after domestic consumption bottomed out in the middle of 1997.

He expected the economy to pick up in the second half of this year, leading to growth in gross domestic product of 1.5 to 2.0 percent for the entire year, offsetting any declines caused by the government's budget-tightening policy.
The benchmark Nikkei average of 225 leading shares stood at 18,201.04 at Thursday midday, after it tumbled close to 17,000 earlier this month.
The Nikkei 225 is expected to continue its volatile movement for the time being because of the weak outlook for the economy and Japan's structural reforms, Tanaka said.
Domestic consumption will bottom out in the middle of the year after the government raises the sales tax to five percent in April from the current three percent, he said.
